extraction.name: Instruction-Following Eval (IFEval)
extraction.description: A benchmark to evaluate the instruction-following ability of large language models using prompts containing verifiable instructions that can be automatically and objectively verified.
extraction.creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The prompts were created by generating base prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions, filtering illogical prompts with few-shot prompting, rephrasing prompts with another few-shot prompting approach, and then manually checking and editing them.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Base prompts with appended verifiable instructions, resulting in a set of 541 prompts and a list of 25 verifiable instructions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Illogical prompts were removed, prompts were rephrased to increase diversity, and responses were transformed during loose evaluation by removing markdown font modifiers, the first line, and the last line, including combinations of these transformations.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The benchmark uses verifiable instructions whose compliance is checked automatically with simple, interpretable, deterministic programs and heuristics, rather than human labeling.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper discusses strict and loose verification, noting that strict verification can produce false negatives and loose verification can reduce false negatives but may introduce false positives.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that instruction-following is crucial for safety and reliability, and failures can have dire results in crucial scenarios like healthcare or autonomous systems.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes potential biases in existing human and model-based evaluation methods and presents IFEval as an unbiased automatic approach.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Very few instructions are fully objectively and automatically verifiable; edge cases remain hard to determine, the current implementation can be improved across many fronts, and the instruction list can be expanded.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation benchmark for measuring the instruction-following ability of large language models and comparing models across instruction types.

name.evidence: To overcome these issues, we introduce Instruction-Following Eval ( IFEval ) for large language models.

description.evidence: In summary, we propose IFEval: Instruction-Following Eval, a benchmark to evaluate the instruction following ability of LLMs using a set of prompts containing verifiable instructions.

url.evidence: Our code and data can be found at https://github.com/google-research/ google-research/tree/master/instruction_following_eval

inLanguage.evidence: One key capability of LLMs is to follow input natural language instructions, also known as zero-shot prompts

isLiveDataset.evidence: We report evaluation results of multiple models, and release our code and prompts used for evaluation

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We alleviate these problems by creating our prompts through four steps. First, we generate a set of base prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions appended to the end of each prompt. Then, we use few-shot prompting to identify illogical prompts and remove them. As the third step, we apply another few-shot prompting based approach to rephrase each prompt, to increase the diversity of phrasing. Finally, we manually check and edit the rephrased prompts one by one.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: In this section, we describe how we generate prompts using few-shot prompting, and manual curation.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Altogether, we create a list of 25 verifiable instructions. We further create a set of 541 prompts, with each prompt containing one or multiple verifiable instructions.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: We scrapped GPT-4 and PaLM 2 S responses in November and August of 2023, respectively, through API calls.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Then, we use few-shot prompting to identify illogical prompts and remove them. As the third step, we apply another few-shot prompting based approach to rephrase each prompt, to increase the diversity of phrasing. We transform each response using every of the following transformation functions: 1. Remove commonly seen font modifiers in the markdown syntax, especially “*” and “**”. 2. Remove the first line of the response, so that we skip intros like “Sure, here it is:”. 3. Remove the last line of the response, so that we skip outros like “Hope it helps.”.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: These verifiable instructions are atomic instructions for which one can use a simple, interpretable, and deterministic program to verify if corresponding responses follow the instructions or not.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: Even though we can verify if an instruction is followed using simple heuristics and programming, we found that there are still false negatives... To alleviate this false negative problem, we compute a loose accuracy score of instruction following... Although this loose instruction-following verification process reduces false negatives, it is likely to introduce false positives.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: The capability of LLMs to accurately interpret and follow natural language instructions is crucial, not only for the precision of tasks but also for the safety and reliability of their implementations. Discrepancies or misunderstandings in following instructions can lead to unintended outputs, which might have dire results, especially in crucial scenarios like healthcare or autonomous systems.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Human evaluation ... is time consuming, expensive and relies on a set of human annotators, leading to potential biases and inconsistencies for reproducibility. ... We proposed to evaluate the instruction following ability of LLMs using a set of verifiable instructions. Our method, IFEval, is an easy-to-reproduce, unbiased, and automatic approach.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: It is important to note that while we focus on verifiable instructions, very few instructions are 100% verifiable objectively and automatically – there always exist edge cases where it is hard to determine if an instruction is followed. ... Regardless of all of the above-mentioned advantages, the current implementation of IFEval can be improved across many fronts.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: In summary, we propose IFEval: Instruction-Following Eval, a benchmark to evaluate the instruction following ability of LLMs using a set of prompts containing verifiable instructions. ... Furthermore, by analyzing the evaluation results, researchers are able to draw insights on what types of instructions are not usually followed, and compare different large language models on various instruction types.
